title: The Anatomy of Socio-Demographics in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling: When and Where It Helps, and the Role of Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.37896v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Subjective judgments such as offensiveness often vary substantially across individuals, motivating pluralistic modeling approaches that incorporate annotators' socio-demographic information to capture this variation. However, prior findings on the benefits of socio-demographic information for pluralistic modeling are mixed, calling for a systematic analysis of both its effectiveness and the mechanisms through which it improves prediction. In this work, we study $\textbf{when}$ and $\textbf{where}$ socio-demographics benefit pluralistic offensiveness modeling, as well as $\textbf{the role of explicit reasoning}$ in leveraging this information. translated_title: 多元化冒犯性建模中社会人口统计特征的剖析：它在何时何地有所帮助，以及推理的作用
translated_abstract: 诸如冒犯性之类的主观判断在个体之间往往存在显著差异，这促使多元化建模方法纳入标注者的社会人口统计信息以捕捉这种差异。然而，关于社会人口统计信息对多元化建模益处的先前研究结果并不一致，因此需要对其有效性及其改进预测的机制进行系统性分析。在本工作中，我们研究了社会人口统计特征在何时以及何处有益于多元化冒犯性建模，以及显式推理在利用这一信息中所起的作用。在三个多标注者数据集上，通过使用提示式和训练式的大语言模型，我们首先表明，人口统计信息对个体预测的增益小且不一致，但在群体和总体层面变得更加明显，因为聚合减弱了掩盖小而系统性差异的个体特有变异……
tldr: 本文系统分析了社会人口统计信息在大语言模型多元化冒犯性建模中的作用，发现其对个体预测的增益小且不稳定，但在群体和总体层面更为明显，并揭示了显式推理在有效利用人口统计信息中的关键角色。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically dissects when and where socio-demographic information benefits pluralistic offensiveness modeling with LLMs, showing that demographic gains are small and inconsistent for individual predictions but become clearer at group and population levels, and elucidates the critical role of explicit reasoning in leveraging such information.
